newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia sees Estonia accord boosting trade.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia sees Estonia accord boosting trade.

text.p: Slovenia's Ministry of Economic Relations and Development said on Tuesday trade with Estonia would continue growing rapidly following a free trade agreement, effective in January.

The agreement, signed on Tuesday in the Estonian capital Tallinn, will abolish custom tariffs on most industrial products from January 1997 and gradually reduce duties on agricultural goods to zero by the year 2002.
Slovenian exports to Estonia largely consist of drugs, plastic floor coverings, paper and cosmetics, while imports include chemicals, wood products, fruit and textiles.
In the first nine months of this year, Slovenia exported $800,000 of goods to the Baltic state, up 29 percent on the same period in 1995. Imports tripled to $400,000.
"The increase of trade was mainly the result of very small trade with Estonia in the past," the ministry said.
Trade with Estonia in 1995 represented less than 0.1 percent of Slovenia's total foreign trade. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana Newsroom, 386 61 1263 644
